title: Section 13B HMA — Divorce by mutual consent

content.overview: Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is divorce by mutual consent. Both parties may present a petition on the ground that they have been living separately for one year or more, that they have not been able to live together, and that they have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved. The second motion is not earlier than six months after the presentation of the petition and not later than eighteen months after that date, if the petition is not withdrawn. The court then passes a decree of divorce if satisfied that the marriage was solemnized and that the averments are true. Waiver of the six-month period is case-law and is not treated as a statutory deletion of that waiting period.
content.study: Require a joint petition, one year of separate living, mutual agreement, and the six-to-eighteen-month second motion. Do not convert a contested section 13 petition into section 13B. Do not treat cooling-off waiver as the text of the section.

learningObjectives: State the six-month and eighteen-month second-motion window.
Keep waiver of the waiting period on the case-law gate.
enhancement.definition: Section 13B is a joint petition for divorce where the spouses have lived separately for at least one year, cannot live together, and agree that the marriage should be dissolved.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Mutual consent must exist at the petition and continue to the second motion. Withdrawal in the meantime stops the decree.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, section 13B. Section 13 is contested divorce.
essentialIngredients: Living separately for one year or more
Second motion after six months and before eighteen months
Court satisfied of solemnization and the truth of the averments
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 13B(1) is the joint presentation. Living separately is a statutory condition of one year or more; its meaning in a given household is not given a case ratio here. Section 13B(2) is the second motion. It cannot be moved before six months from presentation, and it cannot be moved after eighteen months from that date. If either party withdraws consent in the meantime, the court is not in the unwithdrawn-petition case the subsection describes. On the second motion the court hears the parties and makes inquiry, and if satisfied that the marriage was solemnized and the averments in the petition are true, it passes a decree. The six-month period is in the text. Any power to waive it is authority outside this note.
examples: Spouses separated for fourteen months file jointly and agree to dissolve. The second motion is not listed in month two.
One spouse withdraws consent before the second motion. Section 13B(2) does not proceed on an unwithdrawn petition.
A single spouse files on cruelty and asks for mutual consent. Section 13B requires both parties.
enhancement.problemApplication: Check joint presentation, one year apart, continuing consent, and the six-to-eighteen-month window. Leave waiver to the case-law gate.
distinctions: Section 13B joint petition vs section 13 contested grounds
Six-month wait vs eighteen-month outer date
Withdrawal of consent vs a continued second motion
Statutory waiting period vs a waiver claim
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Cooling-off waiver and cruelty tests remain on the case-law gate.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: Both spouses may petition after one year living separately if they cannot live together and agree to dissolve. The second motion is between six and eighteen months, if not withdrawn.

keyTakeaways: Separate living must be one year or more.
The second motion is not before six months.
It is not after eighteen months.
